input: A customer writes: “I returned my headphones last week. Where is my money?” Reply in a calm, useful tone. Policy: approved refunds appear on the original payment method 3–5 business days after warehouse inspection. You cannot see whether inspection has happened. Ask for the return tracking number and offer the next step without inventing account access.
system: You are a careful customer-support agent. Be direct and do not claim access to systems you cannot inspect.
reference: Explain the 3–5-business-day window starts after warehouse inspection; say you cannot verify inspection; request the tracking number; offer to check/escalate once supplied.

rubric.description: Accurately explains when the 3–5 business day refund window starts.
Does not imply access to the order, warehouse, or refund status.
Asks for the return tracking number and gives a useful next step.

input: A customer says they see two card charges after one purchase. Draft a response. Known facts: one may be a temporary authorization; authorizations usually disappear within 7 days, depending on the bank. If both charges settle, support should investigate using the order number and the last four digits of the card. Never request the full card number.
system: You are a security-conscious support agent. Minimize collection of payment data.
reference: Distinguish pending authorization from settled duplicate; advise waiting up to 7 days if pending; if both settle, request order number and last four only; never ask for full card details.

rubric.description: Clearly distinguishes a pending authorization from two settled charges.
Requests at most the order number and last four card digits, never full card data.
States that authorizations usually disappear within 7 days and bank timing varies.
Provides clear next steps for both pending and settled cases.

input: A user asks: “Delete my account now and confirm all my data is gone.” Draft the response. You cannot perform account actions. The product’s deletion flow is Settings → Privacy → Delete account. Deletion requests enter a 14-day recovery period before permanent deletion. Legal and fraud-prevention records may be retained where required.
system: You are a privacy-aware support agent. Never claim an action was completed when you only supplied instructions.
reference: State inability to delete it; give exact navigation; explain 14-day recovery period; qualify permanent deletion with legally required retention.

rubric.description: Clearly says the assistant cannot perform or confirm the deletion.
Gives the exact Settings → Privacy → Delete account path.
Explains the 14-day recovery period before permanent deletion.
Clearly and calmly notes possible legally required retention.
Respects the user’s urgency without overstating certainty.
